# video

Imported as `@elffuss/ai/video`, `@elffuss/ai/video/sizes`, `@elffuss/ai/video/encode`, `@elffuss/ai/video/render`.

## `sdk/video/audio.js`

The soundtrack of a video. Decoding a sound file needs Web Audio, which only exists in a page (not in a Worker): decodeSoundtrack() is the one part of the video task that runs in the page, before the task's Worker gets the samples. fitSoundtrack() is pure: it makes the samples exactly as long as the video, looping a short piece and fading in and out so nothing clicks.

### `SAMPLE_RATE`

The sample rate of every soundtrack (what the encoders take).

### `fitSoundtrack(sound, seconds, { fadeIn = 0.04, fadeOut = 0.6, cross = 0.25 } = {})`

Samples of one channel or two, exactly `seconds` long: cut, or looped with a
short cross-fade when the sound is shorter, then faded in and out.

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `sound` | `{ sampleRate: number, channels: Float32Array[] }` |  |
| `seconds` | `number` |  |
| `[o]` | `{ fadeIn?: number, fadeOut?: number, cross?: number }` | in seconds |

Returns `{ sampleRate: number, channels: Float32Array[] }`: two channels

### `decodeSoundtrack(blob)`

Decode a sound file in the page (any format the browser plays), at
SAMPLE_RATE. Fails with unsupported-format when it is not a sound.

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `blob` | `Blob` |  |

Returns `Promise<{ sampleRate: number, channels: Float32Array[] }>`.

### `soundtrackOf(audio)`

Whatever a caller passes as a soundtrack, as samples: a Blob or File (decoded
here, in the page), an AudioBuffer, or `{ sampleRate, channels }` already.

Returns `Promise<{ sampleRate: number, channels: Float32Array[] } \| null>`.

## `sdk/video/camera.js`

The camera of a video made from one photo: its moves (presets), their easing, where each point of the photo lands in each frame, and the framing that keeps the photo's edges out of the picture. Pure functions: the renderer (WebGL2, sdk/video/render.js) draws with the same numbers, and Node tests them.
 The photo is a surface in front of the camera. Its pixel (u, v), u to the right and v down, both 0-1, has a disparity d (0 farthest, 1 nearest, as the depth model gives it). At the first view every point sits on its own ray, so the photo looks exactly as it is; its distance along that ray is Z = 1 / (1 + relief · (d − focus.d)): the subject (focus) at distance 1, what is nearer closer, what is farther away. Moving the camera then shows the parallax a real camera would see.

### `PRESETS`

The camera moves, in the order the page offers them.

### `DEFAULT_PRESET`

The move used when none is asked for.

### `LOOPS`

Moves that end where they start: the video loops without a seam.

### `ASPECTS`

Aspect ratios of the output, width / height.

### `DEFAULT_ASPECT`

The aspect used when none is asked for.

### `RELIEF`

How strong the relief of the photo is by default (see `relief` above).

### `MIN_DISPARITY`

The farthest a point may be: its disparity never goes under this (Z at most 1 / this).

### `BASE_FIT`

The frame window at the first view, as a share of the largest one the photo allows.

### `COVER_MARGIN`

A little more zoom than the sampled frames need, for the frames between them.

### `MAX_COVER_ZOOM`

The most the framing may zoom in to keep the edges out (beyond it, the move is made smaller).

### `easeInOut(t)`

Ease in and out (sine): 0 at 0, 1 at 1, flat at both ends.

### `easeSmoother(t)`

A smoother ease for long moves (quintic smootherstep): still at both ends, no jerk.

### `worldPoint(g, u, v, d)`

Where a point of the photo is in the world.

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `g` | `{ A: number, relief: number, focusD: number }` | the photo's aspect (width / height), relief and focus disparity |

Returns `[number, number, number]`.

### `projectWorld(view, p)`

Where a world point lands in the frame of a view: x and y from −1 to 1 inside
the frame (y up), and its distance in front of the camera.

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `view` | `{ pos: number[], yaw: number, pitch: number, shift: number[], half: number[] }` |  |
| `p` | `number[]` |  |

### `projectPoint(plan, view, u, v, d)`

Where a point of the photo lands in the frame of a view (see projectWorld).

### `baseWindow(A, r, focus, fit = BASE_FIT)`

The largest window of the photo with the output's aspect, centred as near the
subject as the photo allows. Coordinates are those of the photo at distance 1:
x from −A/2 to A/2, y from −1/2 to 1/2 (up).

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `A` | `number` | photo aspect, width / height |
| `r` | `number` | output aspect, width / height |
| `focus` | `{ u: number, v: number }` |  |
| `[fit]` | `number` |  |

### `MOVES`

The amplitudes of each move at strength 1, in units of the subject's distance
(translations), radians (turns) and factors (zooms).

### `planCamera({ preset = DEFAULT_PRESET, aspect = ASPECTS[DEFAULT_ASPECT], A, focus, relief = RELIEF, strength = 1, borders = [], parallax = [] })`

Plan a move for a photo: its geometry, the window, and the zoom that keeps
the edges of every layer out of the frame for the whole move.

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `o` | `{ preset?: string, aspect?: number, A: number, focus: { u: number, v: number, d: number }, relief?: number, strength?: number, borders?: { u: number, v: number, d: number }[][] }` | `aspect` is the output's (width / height); `borders` are, per layer, points of the photo's edge where that layer shows, with their disparity in that layer (sdk/video/layers.js, borderSamples). `parallax` are limits of the photo: `{ span: [d0, d1], limit }` says that two points of disparities d0 and d1 must never part by more than `limit` (in heights of the photo) during the move; the move is made smaller until they hold (what the painting behind the subject covers, what a surface may stretch). |

### `cameraAt(plan, t)`

The view of a planned move at time t (0-1): camera position, turn, lens shift
and the half size of the frame window at distance 1.

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `plan` | `ReturnType<typeof planCamera>` |  |
| `t` | `number` |  |

### `coverZoom(plan, borders, steps = 120)`

The zoom (1 or more) a plan needs so that no point of any layer's edge shows
inside the frame, at any time of the move.

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `plan` | `ReturnType<typeof planCamera>` |  |
| `borders` | `{ u: number, v: number, d: number }[][]` |  |
| `[steps]` | `number` |  |

### `maxParallax(plan, [d0, d1], steps = 48)`

The most two points of the subject's place, at disparities d0 and d1, part
during a move, in heights of the photo.

### `frameCount(seconds, fps)`

Number of frames of a video of `seconds` at `fps`.

### `frameTime(i, n, loop)`

The time (0-1) of frame i of n. A loop never shows its first frame twice: its
last frame is one step before the start.

## `sdk/video/depth.js`

What the depth model (Depth Anything V2 Small, through ONNX Runtime) takes, read from its preprocessor_config.json: the size (DPT's rule: the side nearest to its scale reaches the model's size, keeping the photo's shape, in multiples of 14) and the normalisation. Pure: Node tests it.

### `depthSpec(cfg)`

The model's input settings, checked.

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `cfg` | `object` | the parsed preprocessor_config.json |

Returns `{ size: number, multiple: number, mean: number[], std: number[], rescale: number, keepAspect: boolean }`.

### `depthInputSize(W, H, spec)`

Width and height the model sees a W × H photo at (DPT: the scale nearest to 1 for both sides).

### `toDepthInput(rgba, w, h, spec)`

Planar float input (1 × 3 × h × w) of RGBA pixels already at the model's size.

## `sdk/video/encode.js`

The exporter: frames (any frame source) and, if given, a soundtrack in, a video file out, with the browser's own encoders (WebCodecs) and the small writers of this module (mp4.js, webm.js). MP4 with H.264 where the browser encodes it, with AAC sound (or Opus where AAC is not offered); otherwise WebM with VP9 (or VP8) and Opus. It works in a Worker or in the page, and knows nothing of photos or cameras: any task that makes frames can use it (a video generated from text, for one).

### `defaultBitrate(width, height, fps)`

Bits per second of the video by default: generous, for a clean picture after a platform re-encodes it.

### `avcCandidates(width, height, fps)`

H.264 codec strings to try, best first (High profile; the level by size and rate).

### `chooseCodecs({ width, height, fps, bitrate = defaultBitrate(width, height, fps), audio = false, audioRate = 48000, container = 'auto', scope = globalThis })`

The encoders this browser offers for a video: container, video and audio
codec configurations, or a reason why it cannot.

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `o` | `{ width: number, height: number, fps: number, bitrate?: number, audio?: boolean, audioRate?: number, container?: 'auto'\|'mp4'\|'webm', scope?: any }` |  |

Returns `Promise<{ container: 'mp4'\|'webm', video: VideoEncoderConfig, audio: AudioEncoderConfig\|null } \| { container: null, reason: string }>`.

### `encodeVideo({ width, height, fps, frames, frame, audio = null, container = 'auto', bitrate, keyEvery = 2, signal, onProgress, scope = globalThis })`

Encode a video.

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `o` | `{ width: number, height: number, fps: number, frames: number, frame: (index: number, timestampUs: number) => (CanvasImageSource\|VideoFrame\|ImageData\|Promise<CanvasImageSource\|VideoFrame\|ImageData>), audio?: { sampleRate: number, channels: Float32Array[] } \| null, container?: 'auto'\|'mp4'\|'webm', bitrate?: number, keyEvery?: number, signal?: AbortSignal, onProgress?: (p: { stage: 'render'\|'mux', frame?: number, frames?: number }) => void, scope?: any }` | `frame` gives frame `index` (0 based); a VideoFrame it returns is closed here. `audio` holds one array of samples (-1 to 1) per channel, already as long as the video; `keyEvery` is in seconds. |

Returns `Promise<{ blob: Blob, mime: string, container: 'mp4'\|'webm', videoCodec: string, audioCodec: string\|null, width: number, height: number, fps: number, frames: number, seconds: number, bytes: number }>`.

## `sdk/video/impl.js`

The image-to-video task where the models run (a Worker, or the page with worker: false). A run turns a photo into its scene (depth with Depth Anything V2 Small, layers cut where the depth jumps, the background behind them painted by MI-GAN) and the scene into a video: the camera of camera.js, drawn with WebGL2 on an OffscreenCanvas (render.js) and encoded with WebCodecs (encode.js). The scene of the last photo is kept, so another move, length or format of the same photo goes straight to the drawing. dispose() releases the sessions and the drawing context.

### `PHOTO_SIDE`

Longest side of the photo kept for each quality (the frames are cut from it).

### `STRETCH_LIMIT`

The most a surface may stretch across the photo's depth during a move, in heights of the photo.

### `REVEAL_SHARE`

The share of the painted band behind the subject a move may uncover.

### `PLAN_SIDE`

Longest side the depth and the layers are worked out at.

### `PREVIEW_SIDE`

Longest side of the scene the page gets for its preview, by default.

### `run(state, input, opts = {}, ctx)`

Run: `opts.output` 'scene' gives the scene (for a page's live preview), else
the video (see index.js, Video.run).

## `sdk/video/index.js`

A video from one photo, in the browser: the photo's depth (Depth Anything V2 Small, Apache-2.0), the background behind what is near painted in (MI-GAN, MIT), a camera that moves through the layers, and an MP4 (WebM where the browser has no H.264 encoder) with an optional soundtrack. The models come from their original Hugging Face repositories at pinned revisions, through the Elffuss model store; everything runs in a Worker except decoding a soundtrack, which needs Web Audio (a page).

### `TASK`

The task name in the registry.

### `pageQuality(env = globalThis)`

The quality 'auto' stands for in this page: standard (720) on a phone, high (1080) elsewhere.

### `class Video`

A video from a photo. Runs in a Worker (replaced after any failure); the first
`load()` or `run()` asks the model store for the files of the variant this
browser can run (WebGPU fp16 with shader-f16, WebGPU fp32, else WebAssembly
q8; MI-GAN is the same file in all) and checks their hashes.

```js
import { Video } from '@elffuss/ai/video';
const video = new Video({ onProgress: p => console.log(p.status, p.stage, p.frame, p.frames) });
const { blob, mime, width, height, seconds, fps } = await video.run(photo, { preset: 'orbit', seconds: 6, aspect: '9:16', audio: song });
await video.dispose();   // the sessions, the drawing context and the Worker
```

Progress events: `downloading` (loaded / total bytes of the models), then
`running` with `stage` 'depth', 'inpaint', 'render' (with `frame` and `frames`)
and 'mux', then `done`. Cancel with `signal`: the Worker is stopped and
everything it held is given back. A second run of the same photo reuses its
depth and layers.

- `.constructor(options)`
- `.run(image, opts = {})`: Make the video of a photo. `image`: a Blob or File (PNG, JPEG, WebP, GIF, BMP or AVIF), an ImageBitmap or an ImageData. Options (plain data; `audio` may also be a Blob, decoded here, in the page): `preset` ('dolly-in', 'orbit', 'swing', 'zoom-pan', 'vertigo'), `seconds` (2-15, 6), `aspect` ('16:9', '9:16', '1:1'), `fps` (24, 25, 30 or 60; 30), `quality` ('auto', 'high' 1080, 'standard' 720), `strength` (of the move, 0.2-2, 1), `effects` ({ dof, vignette, grain }, each 0-1), `container` ('auto', 'mp4', 'webm'), `audio` (a sound file, an AudioBuffer or { sampleRate, channels }: looped or cut to the video, faded out), `signal`. With `output: 'scene'` it gives the photo's layers instead, for a page that previews the moves with createRenderer (see sdk/video/render.js).
- `.scene(image, opts = {})`: The photo's scene for a live preview: its layers (premultiplied RGBA and a disparity plane each), the subject and the edge points the framing keeps out.
- `.estimate(opts = {}, device = 'auto')`: Whether this browser can make a video, and what it would download, before downloading anything. `store` (optional, any object with has(url, bytes)) tells what is already stored; without it `missingBytes` is the whole download.

### `animate({ image, ...args } = {})`

One call, as a chat tool calls it: `animate({ image, preset, seconds, aspect,
audio })` loads the models, makes the video and releases everything. Any
option of `Video` (its constructor's and its run's) goes in the same object.

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `args` | `{ image: Blob\|ImageBitmap\|ImageData } & Record<string, any>` |  |

Returns `Promise<VideoResult>`.

### Type `VideoResult`

```ts
{ blob: Blob, mime: string, container: 'mp4'|'webm', videoCodec: string, audioCodec: string|null, width: number, height: number, fps: number, frames: number, seconds: number, bytes: number, model: string, device: 'webgpu'|'wasm', dtype: string, preset: string, aspect: string, layers: number }
```

What `run()` gives: `blob` is the video file (`mime` with its codecs); `layers` is how many depth layers the photo was cut into.

## `sdk/video/inpaint.js`

What MI-GAN (Picsart AI Research, MIT) is given and what is done with what it paints. The model takes an RGB image and a mask, both bytes, the mask 255 where the photo is kept and 0 where it must paint; it was trained on squares of 512, so the hole is cropped with some of its surroundings and scaled to about that size, and its answer is scaled back and laid only inside the hole, with a soft seam. Pure functions over typed arrays: Node tests them.

### `SIDE`

The side the model works best at.

### `cropFor(hole, w, h, { margin = 0.35, side = SIDE } = {})`

The part of the photo to give the model: the box of the hole, grown by
`margin` of its size on every side (context to paint from), inside the photo,
and the size it is scaled to (longest side SIDE, never enlarged, multiples of 8).

Returns `{ x: number, y: number, w: number, h: number, ow: number, oh: number } \| null`: null when there is no hole

### `resampleCrop(src, sw, crop, ch = 4)`

Box-filter resample of RGBA (or any `ch`-channel bytes) from a crop of a picture to ow × oh.

### `modelInputs(rgba, hole, w, crop)`

The model's two inputs for a crop: the image (1 × 3 × oh × ow, planar bytes)
and the mask (1 × 1 × oh × ow; 255 kept, 0 to paint; any pixel touched by the
hole is painted).

### `composite(rgba, w, h, crop, painted, soft)`

Lay what the model painted (1 × 3 × oh × ow bytes) into the hole of a copy of
the photo, scaled back to the crop (bilinear), blended over a seam of
`feather` pixels at the hole's edge (where `soft` says, 0-1, how much of the
painting shows; by default the hole itself).

Returns `Uint8ClampedArray`: RGBA

## `sdk/video/layers.js`

From one photo and its depth to layers a camera can move through. Where the depth jumps (a person in front of a wall), the photo is cut in two: what is near becomes a layer of its own, with a soft edge that follows the photo, and what is behind it is filled in (MI-GAN paints the colours, sdk/video/inpaint.js; the depth is filled here from around it), only where a real jump of depth can uncover it. planLayers can cut more than once; the task cuts once, which proved the cleanest. Each layer keeps its depth beyond its own edge, so its edge moves with it and never stretches. Pure functions over typed arrays, no canvas: Node tests them.

### `normalizeDisparity(raw, { lo = 0.005, hi = 0.995 } = {})`

Raw model output to disparity 0-1 (1 nearest), robust to a few wild values:
the `lo` and `hi` quantiles become 0 and 1.

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `raw` | `ArrayLike<number>` |  |

### `resizePlane(src, w, h, W, H)`

Bilinear resize of a one-channel plane (pixel centres at half-integers).

### `boxMean(src, w, h, r)`

Mean over a (2r+1)² box, the box clipped at the edges (separable running sums).

### `guidedFilter(I, p, w, h, r, eps)`

Guided filter (He, Sun and Tang): smooths `p` while keeping the edges of the
guide `I`, so a soft map snaps to the photo's edges.

### `toGray(rgba, w, h)`

Luma 0-1 of RGBA pixels.

### `morph(mask, w, h, r)`

Binary dilation (r > 0) or erosion (r < 0) with a square of side 2|r|+1.

### `components(mask, w, h)`

Connected parts (4-neighbours) of a mask: their label per pixel and their sizes.

### `cleanMask(mask, w, h, minArea)`

A mask without its parts smaller than `minArea` pixels, and without holes smaller than it.

### `pushPull(values, known, w, h, channels = 1)`

Fill the unknown pixels of a map from the known ones around them, smoothly
(push-pull: averages up a pyramid of halvings, then back down). `known` is a
weight 0-1 per pixel; `channels` values per pixel.

Returns `Float32Array`: the map, known pixels kept as they were

### `chooseSplit(d, w, h, { known = null, reach = Math.max(2, Math.round(Math.max(w, h) / 120)), minJump = 0.12, minArea = 0.01, maxArea = 0.8 } = {})`

The depth to cut at, if the photo has a real jump: for candidate thresholds,
the mean jump of depth across the edge of what is nearer, measured `reach`
pixels apart. The best one wins if its jump is at least `minJump` and what is
near covers between `minArea` and `maxArea` of the photo.

Returns `{ threshold: number, jump: number, area: number } \| null`.

### `planLayers(d, w, h, { maxCuts = 1 } = {})`

Plan the layers of a photo from its disparity (analysis size): the masks of
what is near (`maxCuts` of them, one by default), each cleaned, far to near.

Returns `{ cuts: { threshold: number, jump: number, area: number, mask: Uint8Array }[] }`.

### `fillBehind(d, mask, w, h)`

Disparity of a map filled where `mask` is set, from the pixels around it (what lies behind).

### `extendOutward(d, mask, w, h, inset = 2)`

Disparity of a near layer: its own inside `mask` (eroded by `inset`, where
the depth model's edge is soft), carried outward beyond its edge so that the
edge moves with the layer.

### `softAlpha(mask, mw, mh, gray, w, h, { radius = Math.max(2, Math.round(Math.max(w, h) / 400)), eps = 2e-3, steep = 1.6 } = {})`

The soft edge (alpha 0-1) of a mask at the photo's size, snapped to the
photo's own edges with a guided filter, then tightened so that it is not
wider than it must be.

### `decontaminate(rgba, alpha, w, h, solid = 0.92, where = null)`

Colours of a near layer where its edge is soft: those pixels mix the layer
with what was behind it, so their colour is taken from the solid inside of the
layer (carried outward), and only their alpha says how much shows. No fringe
of the old background then travels with the layer.

### `borderSamples({ alpha = null, aw = 0, ah = 0, depth, dw, dh }, per = 40)`

Points of the photo's edge where a layer shows (alpha over 1/2), with its
disparity there: what the framing must keep out of the picture
(sdk/video/camera.js, coverZoom).

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `layer` | `{ alpha?: ArrayLike<number>\|null, aw?: number, ah?: number, depth: ArrayLike<number>, dw: number, dh: number }` |  |

### `revealRegion(mask, d, w, h, { reach = Math.max(2, Math.round(Math.max(w, h) / 120)), jump = 0.08, radius = Math.round(Math.max(w, h) * 0.05), grow = 0 } = {})`

Where a near part can uncover what is behind it, and what of it the painter
must not see. `region`: its pixels within `radius` of a real jump of depth (a
neighbour `reach` pixels away and at least `jump` farther), grown by `grow`.
`hide`: the same within twice that radius, so the painter never sees the near
part next to where it paints and nothing of it leaks into the painting.
Elsewhere (where the part is cut from ground that goes on, the same depth on
both sides) nothing behind it ever shows: the layer behind keeps the photo as
it is there, with no painting and no seam, and the painter may read it.
`band` is `hide` before it grows (inside the part only) and `edge` the pixels of
the real jumps themselves.

Returns `{ region: Uint8Array, hide: Uint8Array, band: Uint8Array, edge: Uint8Array }`.

## `sdk/video/mp4.js`

A small MP4 (ISO BMFF) writer for what WebCodecs encodes: one H.264 video track and at most one audio track (AAC or Opus), every sample in memory, the index (moov) before the data so the file plays while it downloads. Samples come in decode order with their presentation time; when the encoder reorders frames the writer adds composition offsets and an edit list. Pure: no browser API, Node tests it by reading the boxes back.

### Type `Mp4Sample`

```ts
{ data: Uint8Array, pts: number, duration: number, key: boolean }
```

`pts` and `duration` in the track's timescale; samples in decode order.

### Type `Mp4Video`

```ts
{ kind: 'video', codec: 'avc1', width: number, height: number, timescale: number, description: Uint8Array, colour?: { primaries: number, transfer: number, matrix: number, fullRange: boolean }, samples: Mp4Sample[] }
```

### Type `Mp4Audio`

```ts
{ kind: 'audio', codec: 'mp4a'|'opus', sampleRate: number, channels: number, timescale: number, description?: Uint8Array, preSkip?: number, bitrate?: number, samples: Mp4Sample[] }
```

### `audioSpecificConfig(rate, channels)`

AAC-LC AudioSpecificConfig for a rate and channel count (when the encoder gives none).

### `writeMp4({ video, audio = null, chunkSeconds = 0.5 })`

Write an MP4 file.

| Parameter | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `o` | `{ video: Mp4Video, audio?: Mp4Audio\|null, chunkSeconds?: number }` |  |

Returns `Uint8Array[]`: the file, in parts (for a Blob)

### `readBoxes(bytes, start = 0, end = bytes.length)`

Read the boxes of an MP4 back (tests and checks): type, size, offset and the
children of the container boxes.

Width and height (even numbers) of the video for an aspect and a quality.

## `sdk/video/render.js`

Draws the layers of a photo seen by the camera of sdk/video/camera.js, with WebGL2, on a canvas of the page (the live preview) or an OffscreenCanvas of a Worker (the export): the same code, so the video is what the preview showed. Each layer is a dense grid lifted by its depth in the vertex shader, textured with the photo (mipmapped, premultiplied alpha), drawn far to near into a multisampled buffer; a last pass adds the finish (depth of field, vignette, grain) and writes the frame. dispose() deletes every object it made and gives the context back.

### `toHalf(v)`

IEEE half-precision bits of a float (for depth textures).

### `halfPlane(values)`

Half floats of a plane of values.

### `gridMesh(w, h)`

A grid of w × h vertices over the photo (u, v in 0-1) and its triangles.

Returns `{ uv: Float32Array, index: Uint32Array }`.

## `sdk/video/webm.js`

A small WebM (Matroska) writer, the fallback when this browser cannot encode H.264: one VP9 or VP8 video track and at most one Opus audio track, every block in memory, clusters that start at key frames, and cues so a player can seek. Pure: Node tests it by reading the elements back.

### `opusHead(channels, sampleRate, preSkip = 312)`

OpusHead for a stream (the codec's own header, as WebM carries it).

### Type `WebmBlock`

```ts
{ data: Uint8Array, us: number, key: boolean }
```

`us`: presentation time in microseconds

### `readElements(bytes, start = 0, end = bytes.length)`

Read top-level elements back (tests): id in hex, size, offset of the payload.
